errno(3) Library Functions Manual errno(3)

NAME

errno - Error stacks and recovery

Function namespace

Public error-state operations use the errno_* namespace: errno_set and its formatted/system-error variants record failures; errno_has, errno_get, and errno_clear inspect and resolve them. Scope, snapshot, import, diagnostic, and shutdown operations share that prefix. SET_ERRNO and the other convenience macros forward to these functions.

The function-symbol rename requires library consumers to rebuild. No legacy function aliases are exported. Existing error types, scope/history types, ASCIICHAT_ERRNO_* constants, and the asciichat_errno.h include path retain their names. General error formatting and statistics functions are unchanged.

Pending errors

Each registered thread has a LIFO stack in a process-wide hash table. The main thread owns process shutdown; workers publish directly. SET_ERRNO() pushes a frame and returns the supplied asciichat_error_t. Returning an existing error propagates it without adding a duplicate. Add a frame only for useful context.

CLEAR_ERRNO() removes one frame. CLEAR_ERRNO_ALL() removes this thread's complete stack. GET_ERRNO() reads the top, or ASCIICHAT_OK. HAS_ERRNO(&snapshot) copies the top. HAS_ERRNO_CODE(code) searches all pending frames, not handled history. ASCIICHAT_OK is never a match. Empty stacks and unknown thread IDs return false.

CLEAR_ERRNO_TID(tid), CLEAR_ERRNO_ALL_TID(tid), and HAS_ERRNO_CODE_TID(tid, code) operate on a full-width platform thread ID. Unconditional TID operations target that ID's current registration. For an inspect-then-clear decision use errno_clear_if_top(tid, generation, error_id); an intervening push, clear, or ID reuse makes it return false. Remote clearing changes only application error state, never another thread's native errno. Automatic TLS destructors unregister exited native threads.

Snapshot ownership

Contexts are self-contained values. They contain a bounded inline message and raw backtrace addresses, not pointers into mutable stack nodes. No snapshot destroy call is necessary. Copies remain valid after pop, cross-thread clear, thread exit, or process registry shutdown. Source locations refer to static compiler strings. Printing symbolizes a private backtrace and frees its symbols.

The context structure and removal of writable TLS globals change the library ABI. Consumers must rebuild against the new header. Replace direct writes to asciichat_errno/asciichat_errno_context with SET_ERRNO or its system-error variant. Replace the old separate cross-thread setter with publication by the offending thread; there is only one authoritative error registry now.

Recovery boundaries

The offending thread owns recovery policy. Libraries record and return errors; application boundaries choose retry, dismissal, connection teardown, or shutdown. 

asciichat_errno_scope_t attempt = errno_scope_begin();
asciichat_error_t result = try_connection();
if (result == ERROR_NETWORK_TIMEOUT) {


    errno_scope_end(attempt, ASCIICHAT_ERRNO_DISMISSED);


    // Retry; errors from before this attempt remain untouched.
} else if (result != ASCIICHAT_OK) {


    LOG_ERRNO_IF_SET("Connection failed");


    return result;
} else {


    ASSERT_NO_ERRNO_SINCE(attempt);


    errno_scope_end(attempt, ASCIICHAT_ERRNO_HANDLED);
}

HAS_ERRNO_CODE_SINCE(attempt, code) searches only frames newer than the checkpoint. Scopes use monotonically assigned IDs and a registration generation, not depth, so concurrent removals cannot cause unrelated older errors to be consumed. errno_checkpoint() observes a suboperation without starting a new causal chain; use it for propagation checks inside an existing attempt. Nested scopes resolve inner attempts independently. Starting an operation also sets a cause boundary: a new failure cannot cite an unrelated older operation.

ASSERT_NO_ERRNO_SINCE detects successful operations that leave newly created errors unresolved in debug builds. It does not clear errors. ASSERT_NO_ERRNO checks the whole current stack. Explicitly resolve known recoverable failures before declaring success; do not blanket-clear caller errors.

For a fatal worker decision, errno_request_exit(code) retains the first nonzero process error independently of stack cleanup. Request normal application shutdown after recording the decision. Main returns that code after the mode has stopped its workers. FATAL remains available for unrecoverable startup failures. A client authentication failure on the server closes that connection, not every other client's session.

Causes, history, and timing

A new frame links to the preceding pending frame inside its operation. LOG_ERRNO_IF_SET prints the chain from outer context toward the original cause. SET_ERRNO produces a debug breadcrumb rather than a separate error-level incident at every propagation layer. Top-level handlers still report failures explicitly.

Every frame has a unique ID, thread generation, captured system/WSA error, wall-clock timestamp, and monotonic creation time. Pending age and resolution latency use only the monotonic clock. SET_ERRNO_SYS captures the system error before evaluating formatting arguments, and macro arguments are evaluated once.

Popped frames become bounded history records with handled, dismissed, thread-exit, or overflow outcomes. Readers can inspect a brief failure even after successful recovery. This is a diagnostic history, not a guaranteed-delivery event queue. Snapshots are non-destructive. History overwrite counters make loss explicit.

Capacity and error-path safety

The process reserves 1,024 frame slots, at most 64 frames per thread, at most 256 registered threads, and 128 history records. Messages hold 1,023 bytes plus the terminator and expose message_truncated. No pending-error allocation is performed on failure, including out-of-memory failures. Pop zeroes and returns a pool slot; thread exit returns all its slots; shutdown zeroes stacks and history and releases the platform TLS key. No message or backtrace-symbol heap allocation remains in the registry.

Two frame slots are reserved for each thread registration, preserving its root and newest error even when other threads exhaust the shared pool. At a depth or shared-pool limit, the second-oldest frame is evicted to preserve root and newest context. dropped_errors counts eviction and failed registration. A registration limit/TLS failure records an overflow history event, but cannot create a pending stack. The original function return code is always preserved.

The registry guard uses platform atomics without recursive diagnostic hooks. Critical sections only manipulate bounded data; logging, handlers, allocation, and backtrace symbolization run outside them. A push becomes visible when it releases the guard. A later synchronized reader sees it unless it has already been popped; history covers that latter case. This is not a wall-clock latency guarantee and the API is not async-signal-safe.

Diagnostics workers

lib/debug/sync.c owns the debug_sync worker for synchronization inspection, deadlock monitoring, and backtraces. lib/debug/stats.c owns the separate debug_stats worker for error totals and memory statistics. lib/debug/errno.c owns the debug_errno worker for all pending thread stacks and handled history. All three serve all five native modes: server, client, mirror, discovery-service, and discovery. Independent deadlines allow delayed requests to coexist. Duplicate requests for the same report coalesce at the earliest deadline. Shutdown wakes and joins all three workers before diagnostic data is destroyed. Signal handlers only set a request flag.

--errno-stacks [TIME] prints pending error stacks, handled history, error totals, and error registry statistics. --sync-state [TIME] prints synchronization state and named registry statistics. Both options are available only in Debug builds. Each schedules its own one-shot report after TIME seconds (immediately when omitted); using both produces two independent reports. Signal and keyboard diagnostic requests notify all three workers; SIGUSR1 includes every pending thread stack. Debug builds monitor synchronization automatically; Release builds do not start the diagnostics workers. Error recording and searching are available in every build. Backtraces follow ENABLE_ERRNO_BACKTRACES.

WASM can call the synchronous printers and debug_sync_poll, debug_errno_poll, and debug_stats_poll from its event loop; it does not create a native diagnostics worker.

Recovery and remote error policy

Use the return value to establish failure. Inspect only errors created by that operation (HAS_ERRNO_CODE_SINCE with a checkpoint/scope) to choose recovery. Resolve that operation's errors only after handling them. Successful independent operations must restore their scope boundary too. Add SET_ERRNO only when adding useful context; propagate the return code unchanged otherwise.

TCP timeouts are retryable only before any header bytes have arrived. A partial header or any payload timeout is terminal. WebRTC retains incomplete packet bytes and returns ERROR_NETWORK_INCOMPLETE while waiting; five seconds from the start of the incomplete packet is a terminal deadline, not reset by another fragment.

Known local packet construction failures may drop a media frame without closing the transport. Send implementations must return ERROR_NETWORK if transmission could have consumed bytes; crypto and unknown failures are not treated as local frame rejections. Optional audio drops are recorded as handled history.

Discovery errors map the ACIP wire namespace to application codes for create, lookup and join. Public responses use an allowlist and generic text; internal paths, subprocess output and backtraces stay local. Session-full and rate-limit rejections use the existing retry budget with bounded exponential delays up to 32 seconds. Authentication/protocol rejections stop automatic retries. Snapshot mode still does not retry.

PROTOCOL_FEATURE_RECOVERABLE_ERRORS (0x04) advertises support for nonfatal audio notifications using the existing protocol version feature field. The server sends an ERROR_AUDIO notification at most once per connection only to an opted-in peer; older peers receive a remote log instead. Video continues on ERROR_AUDIO. Error notifications and logs share the media send lock to preserve packet framing.

Admission captures the original failure before attempting notification. The notification has its own recovery scope, and explicit socket ownership prevents sending on descriptors already consumed by client cleanup. The initial version packet is consumed before a pre-handshake rejection to avoid losing that response to a reset caused by unread input.

The recovery audit covered existing scope/search/clear users across native modes, network transports, discovery, media probes and configuration. It also corrected positive-enum send-result checks and successful-path scope leaks. Legacy APIs with documented negative/status/count returns retain their own return contracts.

Operation-local snapshots and worker handoff

errno_peek_since(checkpoint, &failure) copies the newest error from that operation, rejecting older frames and stale thread generations. Pointer-returning APIs use this to attribute failure without reusing unrelated pending errors.

An operation can store this value snapshot under its own mutex, or publish it through a joined worker result. errno_import(&failure) records a new caller-owned frame with the original error ID as its cause, retaining the copied message, source and raw backtrace even after worker exit or history eviction. It does not consume or clear the producer's errors. Import once when processing an operation result, not by polling arbitrary thread stacks.

ffmpeg_decoder_poll_video distinguishes READY, WAITING, EOF and FAILED; failure includes an owned snapshot. The pointer compatibility API imports FAILED into the reading thread. Capture owners stop on new errors and the pipeline imports its capture failure after joining, so decoder failure cannot masquerade as perpetual frame starvation. Failed prefetch startup fails media creation.

PortAudio software fallback and optional router mapping attempts resolve only their operation scopes. Router renewal failures enter bounded handled history when the scheduler takes responsibility for retrying; mapping state still tracks lease expiration. Rate-limit helpers return a typed status plus an allowed output; connection owners send encrypted public responses under their send lock.

Runtime error popup

While the native terminal presenter is active, newly recorded errors also enter an allocation-free, 128-entry notification journal. The popup shows the symbolic and numeric code, generic meaning, contextual message, system/socket error when present, and originating thread. Debug, Dev, and RelWithDebInfo builds also show the source location and the captured backtrace, using the same semantic formatter as terminal logs. Release hides these developer diagnostics.

Left/Right select the preceding/following error; Home/End select the oldest/newest. New arrivals select the newest error. Up/Down and PageUp/PageDown scroll details. Backtraces use at most 12 visible lines with the shared scrollbar. Error metadata stays fixed while the trace scrolls when the terminal has room for both sections; smaller terminals scroll the combined details so every line remains reachable. The popup displays a Dismiss all button activated by Enter and a ? Help hint. Its compact help overlay lists navigation, scrolling, and dismissal shortcuts. Esc, q, and Enter dismiss all errors and consume the key. Acknowledgment removes only notifications through the captured cutoff ID; concurrent later arrivals remain visible. It never clears a producer's pending errno stack or recovery scope. Overflow keeps the newest 128 notifications and marks older entries as dropped.

The presenter composes the selected screen and retained dialog layers, then errors, then keyboard help. An already open log-viewer help menu also stays above errors. Help retains the underlying interactive selection, including prompts and diagnostics. Below 60 columns or 14 rows the popup uses the common too-small UI; dismissal keys remain active and enlarging the terminal restores selection and scrolling.

Batch output and finite snapshots keep their existing synchronous behavior. UI rendering can suppress its own notifications without suppressing errno storage or logging, preventing recursive popup failures. Normal screen changes intentionally supersede unfinished media frames and are not terminal write errors.

Tests

Build the production library tests without Criterion:

cmake --preset default -B build -DBUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build --target test-errno-stacks
ctest --test-dir build -R "^errno-stacks$" --output-on-failure
cmake --build build --target test-error-popup-fixture
ctest --test-dir build -R "^error-popup-smoke$" --no-tests=error --output-on-failure
python tests/python/integration/errno_smoke/test_smoke.py build/bin/ascii-chat --debug-sync
# Linux: verify SIGUSR1 prints both reports on stdout from separate workers
python tests/python/integration/errno_signal/test_signal.py build/bin/ascii-chat --errno-probe build/bin/test-errno-stacks

Generate a real unsupported-audio fixture with FFmpeg and exercise codec fallback: 

python tests/standalone/errno/codec_fixture.py build/optional-codec.mkv
python tests/python/integration/errno_smoke/test_smoke.py build/bin/ascii-chat --codec-fixture build/optional-codec.mkv

The native suite exercises root/top search, single evaluation, system/WSA metadata, safe value snapshots, scoped recovery, history timing/overflow, thread-ID generations, remote clearing, thread exit, simultaneous writers, global/per-thread capacity, and interruptible diagnostics shutdown. Run test-errno-stacks --assert-leak in a debug build to verify that an unresolved successful-operation boundary exits with ERROR_INVALID_STATE.

The Python error-popup smoke test drives production rendering and input through PTY on POSIX and ConPTY on Windows. It checks journal acknowledgment races, multiple-error navigation, new arrivals under help, dismissal without key replay, scrolling, truncation, control-character sanitization, small/exact-minimum terminal sizes, overflow, colors, monochrome/ASCII output, prompt preservation, and layered status/splash/log/statistics/error-stack/sync/dialog screens where supported. CTest selects diagnostic expectations from the build type. Terminal cell dumps, ANSI streams, screenshots, logs, and result metadata are saved under build/Testing/error-popup (or the corresponding build directory).
